title: A particle in a magnetic field
hook: Change magnetic-field magnitude and predict circular-orbit radius.
misconception: circular-orbit radius doubles when magnetic-field magnitude doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply r = mv/(abs(q)B) to compare circular-orbit radius when magnetic-field magnitude changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a nonrelativistic charged particle at fixed mass speed and charge moving perpendicular to a uniform field, r = mv/(abs(q)B). When magnetic-field magnitude doubles, circular-orbit radius becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model r = mv/(abs(q)B); scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a nonrelativistic charged particle at fixed mass speed and charge moving perpendicular to a uniform field, with a nonzero initial result. If magnetic-field magnitude triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on circular-orbit radius?
recall.why: Apply r = mv/(abs(q)B) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
